subject: Audit logs & data access evidence - next steps
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Chen <alice.chen@fincobank.com>, FinCo Security <security@fincobank.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-03-22T15:05:00-07:00
Subject: Audit logs & data access evidence - next steps

Hi Alice / FinCo Security team,

Thanks again for the time today — helpful call. Quick recap and a set of concrete next steps so we can validate data handling controls and get you a clear mutual action plan.

Call summary (high level)
- Discussed PII and sensitive fields in model inputs and outputs.
- FinCo requires detailed access logging for inference requests and data exports (who/what/when).
- Data residency requirement: production inference and logs must remain in US or EU regions depending on workload classification.
- Retention expectations: FinCo expects auditable retention policy and exports for review.

Requested evidence / acceptance criteria (what would help your compliance review)
1) Audit log export (sample) for the last 60–90 days (if 90 not possible, start with 30 days).
   - Columns: timestamp (ISO8601), user_id (or role), action (e.g., model_call, data_export), object_id/resource, request_id/x-request-id, source_ip, region, bytes_transferred (if applicable)
2) Export formats: CSV or JSON (CSV preferred for initial ingest).
3) Retention policy summary: where logs are stored (region), default retention window, deletion/archival process.
4) Data residency statement for logs and inference payloads.
5) Any supporting artifacts: SOC 2 or internal audit docs, or a short note on how access control and RBAC are enforced.

I've attached our audit log spec (redwood-audit-log-spec.pdf) — it outlines the fields and the export template we typically provide.

Next steps / timeline
- Alice: can you share a sample export (CSV) for review? Even a 30-day slice is fine to start.
- FinCo Security: confirm whether the fields above meet your evidence needs or if additional columns are required.
- We'll aim to ingest the sample and validate mapping within 2 business days of receiving it.

Thanks — happy to sync again if you want to walk through a sample together.

Best,
Ben Carter
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai

From: Alice Chen <alice.chen@fincobank.com>

Subject: Re: Audit logs & data access evidence - next steps

Thanks Ben — appreciate the clear list.

On Tue, Mar 22, 2026 at 3:05 PM Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Hi Alice / FinCo Security team,
> 
> Thanks again for the time today — helpful call. Quick recap and a set of concrete next steps so we can validate data handling controls and get you a clear mutual action plan.

We're attaching a first export: finco-audit-logs-export-20260321.csv. It's a 30-day slice from our logging pipeline (March 1–March 21) — we can request a longer period if needed but want to confirm format first.

What you'll find in the CSV (columns): timestamp, user_id, action, resource_id, request_id, source_ip, region. Timestamps are in UTC ISO8601. Logs are stored in our central logging cluster in us-east-1; default retention is 365 days. Exports can be provided as CSV or JSON.

Question for Redwood: do you need an explicit mapping for our internal system ids (we have alphanumeric service IDs) or is resource_id sufficient? Also, are there any pseudonymization requirements we should follow before sharing?

We can share the file via your secure SFTP or provide a link to a secure share — which do you prefer?

Best,
Alice Chen
Senior Compliance Manager | FinCo Bank
alice.chen@fincobank.com

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alice Chen <alice.chen@fincobank.com>, FinCo Security <security@fincobank.com>
Date: 2026-03-22T16:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Audit logs & data access evidence - next steps

Thanks Alice — that's helpful. A few internal notes and asks to make sure the sample will be usable for our compliance and engineering validation:

- Confirmed columns look good; request_id (x-request-id) is important for end-to-end tracing. If you can include any correlation ids used by your gateway, please add them as a column.
- For resource_id: a mapping table (system_id -> human-readable name) would speed analysis. If that's not possible, include a short legend.
- Regarding pseudonymization: if the CSV contains direct PII, please indicate which columns are PII. We can sign an additional NDA if you prefer a redacted sample first.
- Export integrity: a checksum (SHA256) for the export is helpful.
- Acceptance criteria from Redwood Security for this evidence: 1) proof of access (user/role/action/timestamp), 2) timestamps in ISO8601 (UTC), 3) exported file with header and consistent schema.

Operationally: Marissa, can you own ingestion of the sample once we have the file? I'll coordinate on the compliance checklist and confirm any further asks to FinCo Security.

Linking our internal audit playbook for reference: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1a2b3c-redwood-audit-playbook

Laura Bennett
Security & Compliance Lead | Redwood Inference
